elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered text reads "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT ... EXCEED ...", replacing the one-way "TRUELINK'S LIABILITY" and the broken "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11" scope limit with a mutual, agreement-wide aggregate cap.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cap remains "THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD": no USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, "paid" only (not "paid or payable"), and no anchor to the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The rendered sentence contains no exclusion of indirect, incidental or consequential damages, and the rationale confirms no such language exists elsewhere in the Agreement.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Parenthetical carve-out: "OTHER THAN ... BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS ... WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO ANY LIMITATION".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list names only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; data protection and security obligations are not excluded from the cap.

"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER THIS SECTION 12 ... WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO ANY LIMITATION"; the indemnities identified (including Client's Section 12a indemnity) sit in Section 12, so the reference is not illusory.
Carve-out retains and makes mutual "GROSS NEGLIGENCE ... WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO ANY LIMITATION" (previously TrueLink-only).
Carve-out includes "WILLFUL MISCONDUCT, WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO ANY LIMITATION", now applicable to either party.
No fraud carve-out appears in the parenthetical exclusion list.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out; only Section 12 indemnification obligations are excluded, which does not expressly cover direct IP infringement claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause says nothing about Client's obligation to pay compensation/fees being outside the cap, so accrued payment obligations could be argued to be capped liability.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT" — cap now bilateral and agreement-wide, curing the one-way, Section 3/4/7/11-limited original.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Retained basis: "THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — hosting and support are the services compensated under this Agreement, so this is a genuine 12-month fee basis, not an illusory sub-fee.
"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER THIS SECTION 12 ... WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO ANY LIMITATION".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS" listed among matters "NOT SUBJECT TO ANY LIMITATION".
"GROSS NEGLIGENCE ... WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO ANY LIMITATION", applied to either party.
"WILLFUL MISCONDUCT, WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO ANY LIMITATION".

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single edited sentence makes the cap mutual and aggregate, retains the existing 12-month hosting-and-support compensation basis, and places indemnification (Section 12), confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct outside the cap.

Preferred is not complete: missing the greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable" wording and the "event giving rise to the claim" anchor; no mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion; no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or infringement of the other party's IP; and no statement that Client's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. To reach preferred, the drafter must add these in operative text, not in the comment.

Minimality holds: only the capped-party reference, the aggregate/scope wording and the carve-out parenthetical were touched. Deleting the "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11" cross-reference was necessary rather than cosmetic — those sections do not exist, so the retained trigger was undefined and no true aggregate mutual cap could exist while it stood.

Intent is preserved: the 12-month compensation measure, the existing gross negligence/wilful misconduct exception and the surrounding indemnity architecture survive; the edit removes (rather than creates) a dangling cross-reference and adds no survival tails, procedures or extra damages categories.

Noted for the drafter's awareness (not a defect at fallback): the indemnity carve-out is scoped to "THIS SECTION 12" — confirm no indemnity obligations sit outside Section 12, otherwise broaden to "a party's indemnification obligations under this Agreement".
